The Marqeta DMC API can be integrated in to 3rd party applications to support payment processing in web environments. Implementing the API, developers can manage their users, coordinate payment plans, create spending controls, oversee addresses, fees, campaigns, transactions, transfers, and more. The API accepts HTTP calls in JSON formats, and comes well documented.

name: cheddargetter
description: CheddarGetter is an online billing and subscription management system designed to make it easier to accept and track payments. The CheddarGetter API allows users to integrate the ChedderGetter service into their website or app.

name: heiaheia
description: HeiaHeia is a web and mobile application to track fitness, health, and workouts. HeiaHeia can be used individually, by businesses, and by groups.The HeiaHeia API allows developers to access and integrate the functionality of HeiaHeia with other applications and to create new applications. Some example API methods include retrieving lists of sports, retrieving sport information, managing workout logs, and managing account information.

name: forte-payments-checkout
description: The Forte Checkouts API enables you to make payments on your site with a few lines of code that includes methods for; sale, schedule, token and auth, for Visa, Mast, Amex, Dine and more. It creates a customizable JavaScript button that sits on top of your existing site with Up-to-date customer data, Advanced form field settings and more. Checkouts Pay Now button uses an HTML form POST action with a signature. When the button with coded parameters on the client side is activated, Forte servers read the parameters and populate the modal window. It includes a Forte namespaced version of jQuery that won't conflict with other client-side jQuery code. Forte’s Checkouts supported browsers are Internet Explorer, Firefox, Chrome and Safari. Forte provides a way to build scalable, secure payment applications for In-person, Online, Mobile and Recurring, suite of single source payment solutions for merchants and developers.

name: vantiv-enterprise-eprotect
description: Vantiv's eProtect and OmniToken for Enterprise solutions help solve your card-not-present challenges by virtually eliminating payment data from your order handling systems, transferring the ownership to Vantiv and reducing PCI applicable controls. It controls the fields on your checkout page that hold sensitive card data and includes; Authorize transactions, Sales transactions, Force capture transactions, and more. The eProtect feature is compatible with the following; Native Applications on Mobile Operating Systems, and Browsers; Visa Checkout, Internet Explorer 8, Chrome 1, Android 2.3, Apple iOS 3.2, Windows Phone 10 and more. The eCommerce platform has rich payment processing features that developers can use to build payment enabled applications. Vantiv provides online or in-store payment processing solutions, payment applications for a mobile application, next generation POS, and eCommerce website solutions, for various partners, as well as the customers they serve.

name: google-pay
description: The Google Pay API is used to request credit or debit card information that is stored in a customer’s Google account. It allows you to make online purchases without the need for customers to manually enter any payment information. A payments selection dialog is used to return payment information that is ready to be charged. It uses a supported payments gateway or is directly processed on an encrypted secure server that provides a way to utilize one-touch checkout flows for Google users. Google is a technology company that specializes in Internet-related services and products that includes online advertising technologies, search, cloud computing, software, and hardware. This is indirect access to Google pay, please refer to the available SDK's below.

name: dbs-paylah
description: The PayLah! APIs enables Partners (Merchants) to perform payment request for online checkout, transaction inquiry, refund etc. The documentation showcases all available endpoints and operations for the PayLah! API.You must register for a developer account with DBS (free of charge) to access the documentation. The API is very well documented.DBS (The Development Bank of Singapore Limited | DBS Group) is a leading financial services group in Asia. They are headquartered in Singapore, with a growing presence in Greater China, Southeast Asia and South Asia.

name: dailymile
description: Dailymile is a a social training log for runners, triathletes, and cyclists that lets users create posts about their workouts, map workout routes, and compete with other users. Dailymile provides a RESTful API that lets developers access Dailymile data in their own applications.

name: kwi
description: The Kwi API allows developers to access and integrate the functionality of Kwi with other applications. Public documentation is not available; API access comes with account service. Kwi offers point-of-sale (POS), payment, and inventory solutions for retail businesses.

name: bottomline-technologies-pt-x
description: Bottomline (formerly Albany eVERIFY) provides software for payment processing, bank account validation, direct debit collection and e-document delivery. The Bottomline Technologies PT-X API is a solution that offers accurate validation of bank accounts and sort code details by cross-checking this data against the Extended Industry Sort Code Directory (EISCD). The API enables developers to embed the verification functionality into their existing accounts systems.
